protocol.name: treeland_dde_shell_unstable_v2
protocol.copyright: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2024 - 2026 UnionTech Software Technology Co., Ltd. SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
protocol.description:
This protocol provides DDE desktop components with DDE-specific shell capabilities including surface role management, window overlap detection, active-state notifications, multitask view control, window picking, and lockscreen operations.
The manager global exposes constructor requests for each feature domain. Each constructor returns a separate protocol object with its own lifetime and state.
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.

interface.name: treeland_dde_shell_manager_v2
interface.description:
This global is a factory for the individual protocol objects that compose the DDE shell integration. Each get_* request creates an independent object whose lifetime is controlled by the client via its destroy request.
The client should destroy all child objects before destroying the manager.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the treeland_dde_shell_manager_v2 object.
The client must have already destroyed all objects created through this manager; destroying the manager while child objects still exist is a protocol error.

request.name: get_window_overlap_checker
request.description: Create a treeland_window_overlap_checker_v2 object used to monitor whether a given rectangular region is occluded by xdg-shell toplevels.

request.name: get_shell_surface

description.summary: create a shell surface for a wl_surface

request.description:
Create a treeland_dde_shell_surface_v2 for an existing wl_surface.
At most one shell surface may be associated with a given wl_surface at any time. Attempting to create a second shell surface for the same wl_surface is a protocol error.
The shell surface is typically used in conjunction with xdg_surface to add DDE-specific attributes such as overlay roles, skip-switcher hints, and automatic placement.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: the surface to attach the shell surface to

request.name: get_dde_active
request.description: Create a treeland_dde_active_v2 bound to the given seat. The object emits events when the compositor detects user interaction that affects the DDE active state.

request.name: get_multitaskview
request.description: Create a treeland_multitaskview_v2 that can be used to toggle the multitask (overview) view.

request.name: get_window_picker
request.description: Create a treeland_window_picker_v2 used to request that the user interactively select a window. After a successful pick the compositor sends a window event with the selected window's process ID.

request.name: get_lockscreen
request.description: Create a treeland_lockscreen_v2 that provides requests to lock the screen, show the shutdown UI, or initiate a user-switch operation.

request.name: set_xwindow_position_relative

description.summary: position an XWayland window relative to a wl_surface

request.description:
Request that the compositor move the top-left corner of the XWayland window identified by wid to a position offset by (dx, dy) from the top-left corner of the given anchor surface.
The compositor will send a done event on the provided wl_callback when the operation completes. The callback data is 0 on success and 1 on failure.

arg.name: wid
arg.summary: X11 window ID of the XWayland surface

arg.name: dx
arg.summary: horizontal offset from the anchor's top-left corner

arg.name: dy
arg.summary: vertical offset from the anchor's top-left corner

entry.name: child_not_destroyed
entry.summary: child objects still exist when the manager was destroyed

interface.name: treeland_window_overlap_checker_v2
interface.description:
A treeland_window_overlap_checker_v2 monitors whether a client-specified rectangular region on a given output is occluded by any xdg-shell toplevel.
The client calls update to register or re-register the region of interest. The compositor then sends enter and leave events as the overlap state changes.

enum.name: anchor

description.summary: edge flags for positioning the detected region

enum.description: Bitwise OR of edges that anchor the detected window region to the output. For example, top | left anchors the region to the top-left corner of the output.

entry.name: top
entry.summary: anchor to the top edge of the output

entry.name: bottom
entry.summary: anchor to the bottom edge of the output

entry.name: left
entry.summary: anchor to the left edge of the output

entry.name: right
entry.summary: anchor to the right edge of the output

entry.name: invalid_output
entry.summary: the provided output is invalid or has been destroyed

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_window_overlap_checker_v2 object and stop sending enter/leave events.

request.name: update

description.summary: register or re-register the detected region

request.description:
Specify the rectangular region to monitor and the output on which it resides. The region is positioned relative to the output edges indicated by the anchor bitfield.
The compositor records the window positions at the time this request is processed. If any monitored window moves afterward, the client must call update again to refresh the overlap state.
If the previously registered region is still valid, calling update again replaces it atomically.

arg.name: width
arg.summary: width of the detected region in surface-local coordinates

arg.name: height
arg.summary: height of the detected region in surface-local coordinates

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the output on which the region is located

event.name: enter

description.summary: the detected region is now overlapped

event.description: Sent when at least one xdg-shell toplevel begins to overlap the registered region. Sent at most once per update cycle; the compositor will not send duplicate enter events while the region remains overlapped.

event.name: leave

description.summary: the detected region is no longer overlapped

event.description: Sent when no xdg-shell toplevel overlaps the registered region any more. Sent at most once per update cycle.

interface.name: treeland_dde_shell_surface_v2
interface.description:
A treeland_dde_shell_surface_v2 adds DDE shell attributes to a wl_surface, such as an overlay role, automatic placement, skip-switcher hints, and keyboard focus policy.
The compositor destroys this object automatically when the associated wl_surface is destroyed. The client must call destroy on the treeland_dde_shell_surface_v2 before destroying the wl_surface; destroying the wl_surface first is a protocol error.

enum.name: role
enum.description:
Defines the z-order layer at which the surface is rendered. Currently only the overlay role is available, which places the surface below wlr-layer-shell surfaces at the workspace overlay level.
Multiple surfaces may share the same role; ordering within a single role is undefined.

entry.name: overlay
entry.summary: overlay role, rendered below layer-shell surfaces

entry.name: no_role
entry.summary: a role-dependent request was made before set_role

entry.name: surface_destroyed
entry.summary: the associated wl_surface was already destroyed

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Remove the DDE shell surface role from the wl_surface. The wl_surface becomes unmapped and the shell surface object is destroyed.
This request must be sent before the wl_surface is destroyed.

request.name: set_role

description.summary: assign a rendering role to the surface

request.description: Assign a role that determines the z-order layer. The role may be changed at any time before the surface is destroyed.

request.name: set_surface_position

description.summary: set the surface position in global coordinates

request.description:
Move the surface to the given global coordinates. For example, on a 1920x1080 output starting at (1920, 0), a local position of (50, 50) corresponds to global coordinates (1970, 50).
This request and set_auto_placement are mutually exclusive; calling set_auto_placement after set_surface_position, or vice versa, is a protocol error.

request.name: set_auto_placement

description.summary: let the compositor position the surface below the cursor

request.description:
Request that the compositor automatically position the surface horizontally centered under the cursor at the given vertical offset below the cursor's bottom edge. The compositor also constrains the surface to remain within the output bounds.
This request and set_surface_position are mutually exclusive; calling set_surface_position after set_auto_placement, or vice versa, is a protocol error.

arg.name: y_offset
arg.summary: vertical offset below the cursor bottom edge

request.name: set_skip_switcher

description.summary: set whether the surface should be excluded from the window switcher

request.description: When skip is 1 the compositor should omit this surface from window-switcher UI. When skip is 0 the surface is shown normally. The default is 0.

arg.name: skip
arg.summary: 0 to show in switcher, 1 to skip

request.name: set_skip_dock_preview

description.summary: set whether the surface should be excluded from dock previews

request.description: When skip is 1 the compositor should omit this surface from dock preview thumbnails. When skip is 0 the surface is shown normally. The default is 0.

arg.name: skip
arg.summary: 0 to show in dock preview, 1 to skip

request.name: set_skip_multitask_view

description.summary: set whether the surface should be excluded from the multitask view

request.description: When skip is 1 the compositor should omit this surface from the multitask (overview) view. When skip is 0 the surface is shown normally. The default is 0.

arg.name: skip
arg.summary: 0 to show in multitask view, 1 to skip

request.name: set_accept_keyboard_focus

description.summary: control whether the surface accepts keyboard focus

request.description: When accept is 0 the compositor will not give keyboard focus to this surface, even when it is clicked or otherwise activated. When accept is 1 (default) the surface receives keyboard focus normally.

arg.name: accept
arg.summary: 0 to reject keyboard focus, 1 to accept

interface.name: treeland_dde_active_v2
interface.description: A treeland_dde_active_v2 receives events when the compositor detects user interaction that affects the DDE active state, such as mouse-button presses and scroll-wheel events.

enum.name: reason
enum.description: Indicates the type of input that caused the active state to change.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_dde_active_v2 object and stop sending active-state events.

event.name: active_in

description.summary: the compositor entered an active state

event.description: Sent when the user interaction identified by reason causes the compositor to transition into an active state.

event.name: active_out

description.summary: the compositor left an active state

event.description: Sent when the compositor transitions out of the active state.

event.name: start_drag
event.description: Sent when the compositor begins a drag-and-drop operation.

event.name: drop
event.description: Sent when the compositor completes a drag-and-drop operation, either with a successful drop or a cancellation.

interface.name: treeland_multitaskview_v2
interface.description: A treeland_multitaskview_v2 allows a client to toggle the multitask (overview) view that displays all open windows.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_multitaskview_v2 object. If the multitask view is currently shown it is not automatically dismissed.

request.name: toggle
request.description: If the multitask view is currently hidden, show it. If it is currently shown, hide it.

interface.name: treeland_window_picker_v2
interface.description: A treeland_window_picker_v2 allows a client to initiate an interactive window-picking session. After the user selects a window, the compositor sends a window event with the selected window's process ID.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_window_picker_v2 object and cancel any in-progress picking session.

request.name: pick
request.description:
Request that the compositor enter a picking mode where the user can click on a window. The hint string may be displayed by the compositor to guide the user.
Only one picking session may be active at a time per object; calling pick while a previous pick is still pending is a protocol error.

arg.name: hint
arg.summary: human-readable hint text shown to the user during picking

event.name: window
event.description: Sent after the user completes a picking session to report the process ID of the selected window.

arg.name: pid
arg.summary: process ID of the picked window

entry.name: already_picking
entry.summary: a pick request is already pending on this object

interface.name: treeland_lockscreen_v2
interface.description: A treeland_lockscreen_v2 provides requests to lock the screen, show the shutdown user interface, or initiate a user-switch operation.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_lockscreen_v2 object. This does not affect an already-locked screen or an already-visible shutdown UI.

request.name: lock
request.description: Request that the compositor lock the screen immediately. The compositor may show a lockscreen surface before accepting further input.

request.name: shutdown
request.description: Request that the compositor display the shutdown confirmation UI to the user.

request.name: switch_user
request.description: Request that the compositor present the user-switch interface or switch directly to a different user session, depending on the compositor's session configuration.
